# v1.1.0-dev.69 — One row per setting

Pre-release off the `dev` branch. Builds on `v1.1.0-dev.68`.

A layout fix. The Display editor's monitor rows now follow the
shape Windows 11 uses for its own display settings.

## What Was Broken

Reported with a screenshot. The refresh-rate dropdown was sitting
on top of the "Include small sizes" checkbox, and **By hand** had
been pushed onto a line of its own underneath.

Orientation, resolution, refresh rate, a checkbox, a button and a
badge were all sharing one two-column row. Six things into two
columns wraps into three ragged lines. The dropdown was also wide
enough to spill out of its half.

## What It Looks Like Now

```
Left 1440p · Parsec virtual   \\.\DISPLAY5

  Scaling         [ 100% (recommended)      ▼ ]   now 100%
  Orientation     [ Landscape (current)     ▼ ]
  Resolution      [ 2560 × 1440 (native)    ▼ ]   now 2560 × 1440 @ 60 Hz
  Refresh rate    [ Highest this size offers ▼ ]
                  ☐ Include small sizes   By hand…
```

One setting per row, one control each, labels down a single column,
and the "now" readouts lined up on the right. The two escape
hatches get their own strip underneath instead of competing for
space with a dropdown.

Dropdowns line up across monitors too. They used to size themselves
per card. A monitor with a longer readout ended up with a narrower
dropdown than the one below it, which made the whole list wobble.

The compact picker used by the zoom rules in Settings is unchanged.
It lives in a table cell, where a form would be wrong.

## Install

Auto-updates from dev.53 and later. Otherwise unzip and run.
